name: Trumpeter Hornbill
rangeDescription: Forest of south-central and southeastern africa
description: A large, mostly black-and-white hornbill that occurs in thickets, dense woodland, and riverine and coastal forest. It can be surprisingly inconspicuous while eating large fruit in forest trees, but in flight it has noisy wingbeats and a far-carrying baby-like wailing “whaaaaaa waa waa” call.

name: Laysan Albatross
rangeDescription: Breeds western hawaiian and revillagigedo islands; ranges north pacific
description: A large seabird with very long, narrow wings; much larger than shearwaters and petrels. Unmistakable with white body, dingy pinkish bill, and dark markings on underwing.

name: Shelley's Eagle-Owl
rangeDescription: Sierra leone and liberia to cameroon, gabon, and northeastern democratic republic of the congo
description: Very large, dark rainforest owl. Note the dark brown upperparts, heavily barred underparts, and dark eyes.

name: Yellow-throated Fulvetta
rangeDescription: Nepal to northeastern myanmar, southern china (yunnan), and northern laos
description: Luminous small bird with bright yellow underparts and a lemon-colored brow with thick black borders. Inhabits mid- to high-altitude broadleaf forests, often in openings or edges.

name: Cundinamarca Antpitta
rangeDescription: Eastern andes of colombia (cundinamarca and meta)
description: A rather plain antpitta known only from a small area of Colombia’s eastern Andes, southeast of Bogotá. Plumage is dull brown with small white streaks on the underparts, a slightly paler belly, and a faint eyering.

name: Scott's Oriole
rangeDescription: Arid southwestern usa to southern mexico
description: This black-and-yellow oriole prefers dry habitats where yuccas are plentiful, often on steep hillsides. Males are particularly striking; look for the black back, head, and breast, bright white wingbar, and yellow shoulder.

name: Tumbes Chat-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Arid northwestern peru (tumbes to la libertad)
description: Beautiful little flycatcher found in dry forest in northwestern Peru, and just barely reaching over the border into Ecuador. Striking plumage is distinctive in range; note especially the black mask, yellow eyebrow, and white wingbars.

name: Rosy Minivet
rangeDescription: Himalayas (afghanistan to southwestern china, myanmar, and northern india) to southern china, myanmar, and northwestern vietnam
description: Pale, rather washed-out-looking minivet. Male has a white throat, pink breast, and bright red “apostrophe” on the wing.

name: Blue-masked Leafbird
rangeDescription: Foothills of sumatra
description: The smallest and most unique-looking of the leafbirds. Stout-bodied, with a relatively long, faintly curved bill.

name: Spangled Coquette
rangeDescription: Andes of eastern colombia to western venezuela and northern peru
description: Tiny, short-tailed hummingbird with disjunct range from Venezuela to southeast Ecuador. Spectacular male is mostly green with a bushy orange crest with black spots, a dark throat, a red bill, and a white band across rump.

name: Kenya Rufous Sparrow
rangeDescription: Kenya and tanzania
description: A typical sparrow with a striped back, a gray crown and nape, and a dark bib. The rufous rump is conspicuous in flight.

name: Cryptic Warbler
rangeDescription: Rainforest of eastern madagascar
description: Plain, warbler-like tetraka. Uncommon Madagascar endemic that is found very locally in middle- and high-elevation rainforest.

name: North Island Brown Kiwi
rangeDescription: North island (new zealand)
description: A large, dark grayish brown kiwi with reddish brown streaking. The only kiwi found in the wild on the mainland of New Zealand’s North Island.

name: Lesser Grass-Finch
rangeDescription: Marshes of eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina
description: Large finch with a long spiky tail and strong yellow bill. It is yellow-brown above with dark lines running down the back and pale buff below with a gray face and a white throat.

name: Principe Golden-Weaver
rangeDescription: Príncipe island (gulf of guinea)
description: The only weaver on Príncipe, where it is endemic. Typically yellowish with an olive back: male has a golden-orange wash to the head, while female has a plainer face and a white belly.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Cinderella Waxbill
rangeDescription: Western angola to far northwestern namibia (cunene river)
description: Pretty little gray waxbill with a black tail and a red rump which is conspicuous in flight. The male has red and black under the tail, while the female is much paler and grayer below.

name: Ethiopian Siskin
rangeDescription: Alpine moorlands of northern and central ethiopia
description: An attractive seedeater of the Ethiopian highlands. The distinctive males have a black head and an olive-green and yellow body.

name: Bare-eyed Pigeon
rangeDescription: Arid coastal northeastern colombia to northern venezuela and adjacent islands
description: Large, pale pigeon, unmistakeable if seen well, with large pale blue ocular ring and prominent white wing patches. Occurs in pairs or in small to large groups; mainly seen in trees, tops of cactuses, or in flight.

name: Andaman Green-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Andaman and nicobar islands
description: A large, dull-green pigeon with a thick pale bill and a gray forehead. The dark olive-green and maroon wings have contrasting yellow lines below the shoulders, and the undertail is dull yellow with green patches.

name: Levaillant's Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa
description: A large, dark-backed cuckoo with a floppy crest, white wing patches, and pale underparts; throat and lower flanks both heavily streaked. It is a brood parasite on babblers and other medium-sized birds.
